newsitem.title: USA: Alteon to amend diabetes drug protocol.
newsitem.headline: Alteon to amend diabetes drug protocol.

text.p: Alteon Inc said on Monday a review of its Phase III clinical trial of pimagedine drug, under development to treat diabetic complications, caused it to switch high-dose older Type II diabetic patients with overt nephropathy to a low pimagedine dose.
This change to its so-called ACTION II protocol was made because of dose-related adverse events seen in a number of the older, more fragile Type II diabetic patients, the company said.
No changes would be made to doses administered to younger Type I diabetic patients with overt nephropathy in the ACTION I trial, the company said.

Type I diabetes, or "juvenile onset" diabetes generally affects younger people, while Type II or "adult onset" diabetes, usually affects older people, the company said. Type I diabetics need to take insulin injections, while Type II diabetics do not necessarily need to, the company said.
The ACTION II trial would continue as a placebo-controlled blinded study with no further enrollment of patients, it said.

Alteon also said a review of both trials showed pimagedine was effective in lowering lipids in diabetic patients of all ages. "Both ACTION I and ACTION II trials are showing a statistically significant lipid lowering effect, a relevant marker to the activity of pimagedine," the company said.
